doc.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: How many musicians did the jingle work
summary: About two hundred first-call players did nearly all of it.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: In the same way that you talked about the universe, like ABC, NBC – that’s 175 times 3, which is basically, what? 525 musicians . . .
What would you say was the universe of musicians that was involved in jingles? Was it 100 people? 200 people? 500 people?

In general, that same number – that same group of people who were on staff were generally the ones who were called – on first call of all – you see there were several contractors in town. One contractor couldn’t possibly handle all the jingles. So they had several people who were officiating in the capacity of contractor. All the studios, the first call came off the list. Each studio – there must have been at least 50 people on each studio’s – I would say there were a couple of hundred people who did almost all the work, all the work. It was a very, very lucrative thing
